qe: The Poona Pact (September 1932) was signed between Mahatma Gandhi and B.R. Ambedkar to resolve the issue of:
qh: पूना पैक्ट (सितंबर 1932) महात्मा गांधी और बी.आर. अंबेडकर के बीच किस मुद्दे को हल करने के लिए हस्ताक्षरित किया गया था?
o: Communal representation for Depressed Classes
Complete independence of India
Separate electorates for Muslims
Financial rights of textile laborers
e: Detailed Explanation: The Poona Pact was an agreement between Gandhi and Ambedkar that replaced the provision of separate electorates for the Depressed Classes (as granted by the Communal Award) with a system of reserved seats, while ensuring they remained within the Hindu social fold.

qe: As a result of the Poona Pact, the number of seats reserved for the Depressed Classes in the provincial legislatures was increased from 71 to:
qh: पूना पैक्ट के परिणामस्वरूप, प्रांतीय विधानसभाओं में दलित वर्गों (Depressed Classes) के लिए आरक्षित सीटों की संख्या 71 से बढ़ाकर कितनी कर दी गई थी?
e: Detailed Explanation: Under the Poona Pact, the representation of the Depressed Classes was significantly increased. The reserved seats in provincial legislatures were raised from 71 to 147, and they were also allocated 18% of the total seats in the Central Legislature.

qe: What was the main criticism made by Ambedkar regarding the long-term impact of the Poona Pact on the political empowerment of the Depressed Classes?
qh: दलित वर्गों के राजनीतिक सशक्तिकरण पर पूना पैक्ट के दीर्घकालिक प्रभाव के संबंध में अंबेडकर द्वारा की गई मुख्य आलोचना क्या थी?
o: It made them political tools for majoritarian caste Hindu organizations
It gave them complete administrative control over the Indian police
It led to their total exclusion from the constitutional assembly
It forced them to migrate permanently to Burma
e: Detailed Explanation: Ambedkar criticized the Pact for making Dalits 'political tools' of majoritarian Hindu organizations, as reserved seats often led to the election of representatives supported by caste Hindu parties rather than genuine, independent Dalit leaders.

qe: Mahatma Gandhi set up the 'All India Anti-Untouchability League' in which year to combat the social evil of untouchability?
qh: महात्मा गांधी ने अस्पृश्यता की सामाजिक बुराई से लड़ने के लिए किस वर्ष 'अखिल भारतीय अस्पृश्यता विरोधी लीग' (All India Anti-Untouchability League) की स्थापना की थी?
e: Detailed Explanation: While in Yerwada jail in September 1932, Gandhi established the All India Anti-Untouchability League, which was later renamed the Harijan Sevak Sangh.

qe: Gandhi launched the weekly journal 'Harijan' in January 1933 to propagate his views on social reform. Where did he shift his base after his release from jail in 1933?
qh: गांधी ने जनवरी 1933 में सामाजिक सुधार पर अपने विचारों का प्रचार करने के लिए 'हरिजन' साप्ताहिक पत्रिका शुरू की। 1933 में जेल से रिहा होने के बाद उन्होंने अपना आधार कहाँ स्थानांतरित किया?
o: Satyagraha Ashram, Wardha
Sabarmati Ashram, Ahmedabad
Yerwada Jail, Poona
Delhi
e: Detailed Explanation: After being released from jail in 1933, Gandhi did not return to Sabarmati Ashram, as he had vowed not to return until Swaraj was won. He shifted to the Satyagraha Ashram in Wardha.

qe: Gandhi’s Harijan tour, conducted between 1933 and 1934, covered approximately how many kilometers?
qh: 1933 और 1934 के बीच आयोजित गांधी के 'हरिजन टूर' ने लगभग कितने किलोमीटर की दूरी तय की?
e: Detailed Explanation: Gandhi undertook a massive country-wide Harijan tour from November 1933 to July 1934, covering nearly 20,000 km to collect funds for the Harijan Sevak Sangh and propagate the removal of untouchability.

qe: Which famous slogan did Gandhi use to emphasize the existential urgency of removing untouchability from Hindu society?
qh: गांधी ने हिंदू समाज से अस्पृश्यता को दूर करने की तात्कालिकता पर जोर देने के लिए किस प्रसिद्ध नारे का उपयोग किया?
o: Hinduism dies if untouchability lives, untouchability has to die if Hinduism is to live
Swaraj is my birthright
Do or Die
Inquilab Zindabad
e: Detailed Explanation: Gandhi viewed untouchability as a 'moral stigma' on Hinduism. He famously stated, 'Hinduism dies if untouchability lives; untouchability has to die if Hinduism is to live,' emphasizing that its survival was incompatible with a reformed religion.

qe: Regarding the caste system, how did the ideological position of Gandhi differ from that of B.R. Ambedkar?
qh: जाति व्यवस्था के संबंध में, गांधी की वैचारिक स्थिति बी.आर. अंबेडकर से किस प्रकार भिन्न थी?
o: Gandhi distinguished between the abolition of untouchability and the caste system itself, whereas Ambedkar advocated for the annihilation of the caste system
Gandhi wanted to enforce hereditary occupations through constitutional law
Ambedkar was a staunch supporter of the chaturvarna system based on birth
Gandhi believed caste was never part of Hinduism
e: Detailed Explanation: Gandhi initially focused on purging the 'high-low' distinctions from the varna system, believing varna could be complementary. Ambedkar, however, believed the caste system itself was the root of untouchability and demanded its total annihilation.

qe: B.R. Ambedkar believed that Indian unity was a by-product of which administrative factor, contradicting Gandhi's view that India was a nation since ancient times?
qh: बी.आर. अंबेडकर का मानना था कि भारतीय एकता किस प्रशासनिक कारक का उप-उत्पाद (by-product) थी, जो गांधी के इस विचार के विपरीत था कि भारत प्राचीन काल से ही एक राष्ट्र है?
o: The legal system introduced by the imperial state
The spread of Sanskrit scriptures by high-caste priests
The ancient geographical continuity of the Himalayan borders
The common economic trade routes established during the Mughal era
e: Detailed Explanation: Ambedkar argued that India became a unified entity primarily due to the common legal and administrative system introduced by British colonial rule, while Gandhi emphasized that India possessed an ancient, inherent cultural and national unity.

qe: Both Gandhi and Ambedkar held similar stances on the role of religion in society. Which of the following statements reflects their shared belief?
qh: गांधी और अंबेडकर दोनों ने समाज में धर्म की भूमिका पर समान रुख रखा था। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन उनके साझा विश्वास को दर्शाता है?
o: Both accepted religion as an agent of social change
Both believed that religion should have no place in political life
Both agreed that scripture should be treated as infallible and static
Both believed that state-sponsored religious conversion was the only path to equality
e: Detailed Explanation: Despite their differences, both leaders recognized the potential of religion as a powerful agent for social transformation and integration, provided it was purged of oppressive practices.

qe: What fundamental difference existed in their perceptions of machinery and industrialization?
qh: मशीनीकरण और औद्योगीकरण के प्रति उनकी धारणाओं में क्या मौलिक अंतर था?
o: Gandhi feared the dehumanizing impact of mechanization, whereas Ambedkar believed machinery was essential for a democratic society
Ambedkar feared machinery would destroy rural handicrafts, whereas Gandhi promoted heavy steel factories
Gandhi wanted to make India a global hub for heavy weaponry, while Ambedkar preferred cottage industries
There was no difference, as both supported the absolute prohibition of all modern manufacturing technologies
e: Detailed Explanation: Gandhi was deeply skeptical of heavy machinery, fearing it would lead to deindustrialization and unemployment in rural India. Conversely, Ambedkar famously believed that for India to progress as a democratic society, the slogan must be 'machinery and more machinery'.

qe: Which of the following books authored by B.R. Ambedkar was burned by him in 1927 at Mahad as a symbolic act against caste inequality?
qh: बी.आर. अंबेडकर द्वारा लिखित किस पुस्तक को उन्होंने 1927 में महाद में जातिगत असमानता के खिलाफ एक प्रतीकात्मक कार्य के रूप में जलाया था?
o: Manusmriti
Gulamgiri
Sarvajanik Satyadharma
Satyarth Prakash
e: Detailed Explanation: During the Mahad Satyagraha, Ambedkar and his followers publicly burned the Manusmriti, which they viewed as the canonical source of caste-based discrimination and untouchability.

qe: During his anti-untouchability campaign, Gandhi was constantly attacked by orthodox elements (Sanatanis). What measure did the government take that pleased these orthodox groups?
qh: अपनी अस्पृश्यता विरोधी मुहिम के दौरान, गांधी पर रूढ़िवादी तत्वों (सनातनियों) द्वारा लगातार हमले किए गए। सरकार ने कौन सा कदम उठाया जिससे ये रूढ़िवादी समूह प्रसन्न हुए?
o: They defeated the Temple Entry Bill in August 1934
They declared all caste Hindus to be legally untouchable
They passed a law mandating the segregation of all dalits into independent villages
They made the study of Vedas compulsory for all citizens
e: Detailed Explanation: The government often used orthodox Hindu sentiment to check the Congress movement. By defeating the Temple Entry Bill in 1934, they successfully aligned with the reactionary elements who were opposed to Gandhi's social reform agenda.

qe: Gandhi's concept of 'Gramraj' was challenged by Ambedkar on what structural ground?
qh: अंबेडकर द्वारा गांधी की 'ग्रामराज' (Gramraj) की अवधारणा को किस संरचनात्मक आधार पर चुनौती दी गई थी?
o: Ambedkar believed that Indian villages were nests of local caste-based inequality and discrimination
He thought that Gramraj would reduce the military power of the central state
He argued that Gramraj lacked any provision for English-medium education
He believed that rural areas were too wealthy and did not require any government assistance
e: Detailed Explanation: Ambedkar was a harsh critic of the Indian village system. He argued that the rural social structure was dominated by status quoist hierarchies and that decentralizing power to villages would only strengthen the existing oppressive caste system.

qe: In the later phase of his life, Ambedkar took a radical step regarding his religious identity. What was this step?
qh: अपने जीवन के उत्तरार्ध में, अंबेडकर ने अपनी धार्मिक पहचान के संबंध में एक क्रांतिकारी कदम उठाया। यह कदम क्या था?
o: He denounced Hinduism and converted to Buddhism
He converted to Christianity to access missionary hospitals
He took a vow to strictly follow the Vedas
He declared himself the official head of the Sanatana Dharma Sabha
e: Detailed Explanation: Convinced that the caste system and untouchability were inherent to the Hindu religious scriptures and could not be reformed from within, Ambedkar ultimately renounced Hinduism and embraced Buddhism in 1956.

qe: What was the main difference in the communication methods of Gandhi and Ambedkar?
qh: गांधी और अंबेडकर के संचार के तरीकों में मुख्य अंतर क्या था?
o: Gandhi spoke in plain local vernacular, whereas Ambedkar spoke in English
Ambedkar used traditional folk songs while Gandhi spoke only in Latin
Gandhi used secret codes for his speeches, whereas Ambedkar used official press releases
Ambedkar promoted Sanskrit ritual chanting, while Gandhi used only Urdu
e: Detailed Explanation: Their methods of mass mobilization differed significantly. Gandhi's message was disseminated through the plain local vernacular (Hindustani/Gujarati), making him accessible to the masses. Ambedkar, with his academic background, primarily communicated his vision through English, addressing a different tier of educated political thought.

qe: Which event is considered the 'kindergarten stage of revolution' by an English journalist, comparing the overthrow of a colonial empire by boiling sea-water?
qh: किस घटना को एक अंग्रेज पत्रकार ने 'क्रांति का किंडरगार्टन चरण' (kindergarten stage of revolution) माना है, जिसमें समुद्र के पानी को उबालकर एक औपनिवेशिक साम्राज्य को उखाड़ने की तुलना की गई है?
o: Dandi March
Ahmedabad Mill Strike
Jallianwala Bagh Massacre
Champaran Satyagraha
e: Detailed Explanation: The English journalist Brailsford famously mocked the Dandi March by calling it the 'kindergarten stage of revolution,' incredulously asking how the British Emperor could be unseated simply by boiling sea-water in a kettle.

qe: What was the official British response to the demands of the 'Minorities' Pact' at the Second Round Table Conference?
qh: द्वितीय गोलमेज सम्मेलन में 'अल्पसंख्यक समझौते' (Minorities' Pact) की मांगों के प्रति ब्रिटिश सरकार की आधिकारिक प्रतिक्रिया क्या थी?
o: The government used these diverse demands to neutralize Gandhi's leadership and claimed Congress did not represent all of India
They immediately accepted all demands and signed a binding treaty
They completely ignored the existence of the pact and focused only on industrial quotas
They ordered the immediate arrest of every Parsi delegate present
e: Detailed Explanation: The British government utilized the conflicting demands of the various delegates (Muslims, Depressed Classes, etc.) to claim that the Congress was not a representative body. This helped them stall constitutional progress by focusing on the communal deadlock.

qe: During the Civil Disobedience Movement, which region in the Central Provinces was specifically targeted for the violation of forest laws?
qh: सविनय अवज्ञा आंदोलन के दौरान, वन कानूनों (forest laws) के उल्लंघन के लिए मध्य प्रांत (Central Provinces) के किस क्षेत्र को विशेष रूप से लक्षित किया गया था?
o: Central Provinces tribal tracts
Barhee region of Munger
Saran forest belts
The urban municipal parks of Ahmedabad
e: Detailed Explanation: Adapting to regional conditions, the Congress leadership in the Central Provinces launched a specific campaign focused on the systematic violation of colonial forest laws, which prevented tribal populations from accessing timber and grazing lands.

qe: How did Gandhi define 'Swaraj' in his political text 'Hind Swaraj'?
qh: गांधी ने अपने राजनीतिक ग्रंथ 'हिंद स्वराज' (Hind Swaraj) में 'स्वराज' को कैसे परिभाषित किया?
o: He argued that India was a nation prior to imperial rule and it was the British who broke this cultural unity
He suggested that Swaraj could only be achieved through military conquest by native industrialist classes
He defined Swaraj as the right to demand separate electorates for high-caste landlords
He claimed that the Indian village system was the primary obstacle to national independence
e: Detailed Explanation: In 'Hind Swaraj', Gandhi countered colonial narratives that India was a collection of disorganized tribes. He argued that India had possessed a robust national and cultural identity long before the British arrived and that foreign rule systematically destroyed this underlying unity.

qe: Which of the following was a structural achievement of the Swarajists inside the legislative chambers during their period of parliamentary activity?
qh: विधायी कक्षों में अपने संसदीय गतिविधि के चरण के दौरान स्वराजवादियों की कौन सी संरचनात्मक उपलब्धि थी?
o: The defeat of the Public Safety Bill in 1928
The complete physical destruction of the central Imperial Legislative Council building
The mandatory recruitment of all swadeshi textile factory workers into the provincial councils
The direct legal transfer of the Viceroy's executive council power to the Indian League front
e: Detailed Explanation: One of the most noteworthy achievements of the Swarajists in the Central Legislative Assembly was the defeat of the Public Safety Bill in 1928, which the government aimed to use to deport foreign activists and suppress the spread of socialist ideology.

qe: The 'Act for Better Government of India, 1858' introduced a profound constitutional shift in the administrative structure of the sub-continent by executing which measure?
qh: ऐतिहासिक 'Act for Better Government of India, 1858' ने कौन सा उपाय करके उपमहाद्वीप के प्रशासनिक ढांचे में एक गहरा संवैधानिक बदलाव पेश किया था?
o: Transferring the power to govern from the East India Company directly to the British Crown, to be wielded through a Secretary of State
Establishing complete provincial autonomy under popular native ministerial portfolios
Abolishing the office of the Viceroy and creating the separate Federal Court structure at Allahabad
Scrapping the supervisory control of the British Parliament over Indian revenues
e: Detailed Explanation: The Act of 1858 dissolved the East India Company. It transferred the sovereign power to govern India directly to the British Crown, to be exercised through a cabinet post, the Secretary of State for India, who was assisted by a 15-member council and made directly answerable to the British Parliament.

qe: What macro-level transformation occurred to India's dynamic share of global manufacturing exports across the centuries of British colonial rule?
qh: ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक शासन के सदियों के दौरान वैश्विक विनिर्माण निर्यात (world manufacturing exports) में भारत कीं गतिशील हिस्सेदारी में बड़े पैमाने पर क्या परिवर्तन आया?
o: It dramatically fell from 27 per cent down to a mere 2 per cent
It increased steadily from 2 per cent up to an optimized 27 per cent
It remained perfectly constant at a balanced 10 per cent layout
It dropped to zero instantly within the first decade of the Charter Act of 1813
e: Detailed Explanation: As highlighted by modern economic historians, the systemic deindustrialization and forced commercialization under British rule caused India's share of world manufacturing exports to crash from a dominant 27 per cent down to a mere 2 per cent by the end of the colonial era.

qe: The judicial framework of the Cornwallis Code of 1793 established a major milestone in modern Indian administrative history by firmly introducing which concept?
qh: 1793 के 'कॉर्नवॉलिस कोड' ने किस प्रमुख अवधारणा को दृढ़ता से पेश करके आधुनिक भारतीय प्रशासनिक इतिहास में एक बुनियादी मील का पत्थर स्थापित किया?
o: The principle of the sovereignty of law and the separation of revenue and justice administration
The absolute legal immunity of all colonial government officials from civil court oversight
The mandatory use of English instead of vernacular languages across all local lower subdivisions
The total structural centralization of all judicial functions under the district Collector
e: Detailed Explanation: The Cornwallis Code of 1793 was a landmark because it established the sovereignty of law and the separation of powers. It separated revenue administration from justice, divested the Collector of judicial duties, and made government officials answerable to civil courts for official actions.

qe: In 1860, a judicial modification regulated the privileges of European subjects in India. What restriction did it place on judges of Indian origin regarding criminal cases?
qh: 1860 में, एक न्यायिक संशोधन ने भारत में यूरोपीय विषयों के विशेषाधिकारों को विनियमित किया। इसने आपराधिक मामलों के संबंध में भारतीय मूल के न्यायाधीशों पर कौन सा प्रतिबंध लगाया था?
o: No judge of an Indian origin could legally try a European subject in a criminal case
Indian judges were stripped of any original jurisdiction over civil property disputes involving Europeans
They were legally forced to refer all native criminal files directly to the local Munsiff benches
Indian judges were required to pass all their sentences strictly in classical European ciphers
e: Detailed Explanation: Reflecting the deeply rooted racial discrimination within the colonial legal architecture, a judicial regulation enacted in 1860 specified that while European subjects were brought under court jurisdiction, no judge of Indian origin possessed the legal authority to try a European subject in a criminal case.

qe: Under the central executive guidelines of the Government of India Act, 1919, what specific bicameral houses replaced the old unicameral Imperial Legislative Council?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1919 के केंद्रीय कार्यकारी दिशानिर्देशों के तहत, किन विशिष्ट द्विसदनीय सदनों ने पुरानी एकसदनीय इंपीरियल लेजिस्लेटिव काउंसिल का स्थान लिया?
o: The Central Legislative Assembly (lower house) and the Council of State (upper house)
The House of Commons and the House of Lords structural branches
The British Indian Association and the All India Kisan Sabha chambers
The Sadar Diwani Adalat and the Sadar Nizamat legislative divisions
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1919 Act introduced a bicameral central legislature consisting of a lower house named the Central Legislative Assembly and an upper house named the Council of State, introducing the initial structural principle of a double-chamber parliament.

qe: The Royal Commission on Decentralization (1908) made a critical recommendation regarding the financial and administrative responsibilities of urban municipalities. What role did it suggest they should play in primary education?
qh: रॉयल कमीशन ऑन विकेंद्रीकरण (1908) ने शहरी नगर पालिकाओं की वित्तीय और प्रशासनिक जिम्मेदारियों के संबंध में एक महत्वपूर्ण सिफारिश की थी। इसने प्राथमिक शिक्षा में उनकी क्या भूमिका सुझाया था?
o: The municipalities might explicitly undertake the responsibility for primary education and, if willing, for middle vernacular schools
They should be completely barred from funding or managing any primary-level educational facilities locally
They were legally forced to route 100% of their primary school tax revenues directly to the Dayal Singh Trust in Lahore
The Commission suggested that municipalities should manage only high-cost advanced technical engineering universities
e: Detailed Explanation: To optimize local governance, the 1908 Decentralization Commission recommended that urban municipalities should explicitly take over the responsibility for funding and administering primary education and, if willing, middle vernacular schools, while being relieved of secondary education burdens.

qe: What retrogressive evaluation did the Simon Commission outline in its May 1930 report regarding the efficiency and financial management of local self-governing bodies since 1919?
qh: साइमन कमीशन ने मई 1930 की अपनी रिपोर्ट में 1919 के बाद से स्थानीय स्वशासी निकायों के कुशल और वित्तीय प्रबंधन के संबंध में कौन सा प्रतिगामी (retrogressive) मूल्यांकन प्रस्तुत किया था?
o: It claimed that the management of finances had deteriorated, and suggested the retrograde step of increasing provincial bureaucratic control over local bodies
It celebrated the village panchayats for successfully achieving absolute financial independence across all provinces
It demanded that 100% of local tax revenues must be channeled directly to support the All India Kisan Sabha
The Commission recommended the complete permanent legal abolition of the office of the district magistrate
e: Detailed Explanation: The Simon Commission (May 1930) noted that the financial management of local bodies had deteriorated since the introduction of the 1919 reforms, pointing out a lack of progress in village panchayats. Instead of expanding democracy, it recommended a retrograde step: increasing tight provincial bureaucratic control over these local bodies in the name of efficiency.

qe: What was the significance of the resolution on 'Fundamental Rights' passed at the 1931 Karachi Congress session?
qh: 1931 के कराची कांग्रेस सत्र में पारित 'मौलिक अधिकारों' (Fundamental Rights) के प्रस्ताव का महत्व क्या था?
o: It guaranteed free speech, free press, universal adult franchise, and state neutrality in religious matters
It formally restricted the voting rights exclusively to wealthy aristocratic landowners
It established the British managing agencies as the ultimate authority over Indian education
It mandated the compulsory use of foreign textiles inside all public government offices
e: Detailed Explanation: The Karachi resolution provided the first blueprint of the rights Congress sought to guarantee in a free India, including universal adult franchise, equality before the law, freedom of speech/press, and secularism.

qe: During the mid-1920s, the internal unity of the Swarajist Party fractured along a communal and strategic divide. What were the two competing camps that emerged within the party?
qh: 1920 के दशक के मध्य के दौरान, स्वराजवादी पार्टी की आंतरिक एकता सांप्रदायिक और रणनीतिक विभाजन के कारण टूट गई। पार्टी के भीतर उभरने वाले दो प्रतिस्पर्धी खेमे कौन से थे?
o: The Responsivists and the Non-responsivists
The Moderates and the Extremists structural wings
The Atmiya Sabha and the Dharma Sabha coalitions
The Akali satyagrahis and the Udasi mahant loyalists
e: Detailed Explanation: The Swarajist front fractured into two camps: the 'Responsivists', who favored cooperating with the government to hold offices and protect Hindu interests, and the main leadership ('Non-responsivists'), who rejected government posts and stuck to obstructionist lines.

qe: The British Secretary of State for India, Edwin Montagu, issued a historic statement in August 1917. What did this declaration designate as the ultimate long-term goal of British policy in India?
qh: भारत के ब्रिटिश राज्य सचिव एडविन मोंटेग्यू ने अगस्त 1917 में एक ऐतिहासिक बयान जारी किया था। इस घोषणा ने भारत में ब्रिटिश नीति के अंतिम दीर्घकालिक लक्ष्य के रूप में किसे नामित किया था?
o: The progressive realization of responsible self-government for the people of India
The permanent administrative annexation of all independent princely states directly to the Crown
The complete structural termination of any Indian representation inside executive councils
The mandatory introduction of centralized non-competitive allosteric inhibitors inside all schools
e: Detailed Explanation: Pressured by the nationalist upsurge, Edwin Montagu issued the August 1917 Declaration, which officially committed the British government to the gradual development of self-governing institutions and the progressive realization of responsible government in India.

qe: Which of the following constitutional decisions was NOT taken during the historic December 1929 Lahore session of the Indian National Congress?
qh: भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस के ऐतिहासिक दिसंबर 1929 के लाहौर सत्र के दौरान निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा संवैधानिक निर्णय नहीं लिया गया था?
o: To accept the invitation to participate fully in the upcoming London Round Table Conference
Complete independence was formally declared as the ultimate aim of the Congress
The Congress Working Committee was authorized to launch a program of civil disobedience including non-payment of taxes
All members of the colonial legislatures were asked to immediately resign their seats
e: Detailed Explanation: The Lahore session took highly radical steps: it officially resolved to completely boycott the Round Table Conference, declared Purna Swaraj (complete independence) as its sole objective, authorized a civil disobedience and tax revolt campaign, and ordered all legislators to resign.

qe: Which legendary young woman revolutionary died heroically while actively conducting a daring armed raid on the Pahartali European Club in Chittagong?
qh: चटगाँव में पहाड़तली यूरोपीय क्लब (Pahartali European Club) पर एक साहसिक सशस्त्र छापे को सक्रिय रूप से अंजाम देते समय किस महान युवा महिला क्रांतिकारी की वीरतापूर्ण मृत्यु हो गई थी?
o: Pritilata Waddedar
Kalpana Dutt
Santi Ghosh
Bina Das
e: Detailed Explanation: Pritilata Waddedar led a successful armed attack on the racially discriminatory Pahartali European Club in September 1932. Surrounded by police and injured during the escape, she swallowed potassium cyanide to avoid capture, achieving martyrdom.

qe: During the anti-Rowlatt agitations, what was the primary political transformation regarding the social base of the Indian National Movement?
qh: रौलट-विरोधी आंदोलनों के दौरान भारतीय राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन के सामाजिक आधार के संबंध में प्राथमिक राजनीतिक परिवर्तन क्या था?
o: The orientation of the national movement turned to the masses permanently, involving peasants, artisans, and the urban poor
The movement restricted its focus exclusively to sending long written petitions to the British Parliament
The leadership parameter shifted entirely to favor the wealthy pro-British merchants based in London
The movement abandoned its political character to operate solely as a network of agricultural banks
e: Detailed Explanation: The Rowlatt Satyagraha was a watershed moment. It permanently shifted the focus of the national movement from urban elitist constitutional debates to the masses, bringing peasants, artisans, and the urban poor into active politics under Gandhi's leadership.

qe: A logistic tracking route maps out an exact right-angled triangular course from central base O. A transport vehicle travels 28 km North, and then shifts orientation to drive 21 km East to reach target delivery spot D. Find the absolute straight-line distance from O to D.
qh: एक कार डिपो O से 28 किमी उत्तर की ओर चलती है, और फिर दिशा बदलकर पूर्व की ओर 21 किमी जाकर गंतव्य D पर पहुँचती है। O से D की सीधी रेखा की दूरी ज्ञात कीजिए।
o: 35 km
49 km
42 km
38 km
e:
Detailed Explanation: This spatial path forms a right-angled triangle with perpendicular legs measuring 28 km and 21 km. The straight-line distance is the hypotenuse.
Applying the Pythagoras theorem: $\text{Distance} = \sqrt{28^2 + 21^2} = \sqrt{784 + 441} = \sqrt{1225} = \mathbf{35\text{ km}}$.

qe: The Government of India Act, 1935, proposed the formation of an 'All India Federation'. Which of the following conditions was a prerequisite for its formation?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1935 ने एक 'अखिल भारतीय महासंघ' (All India Federation) के गठन का प्रस्ताव दिया था। इसके गठन के लिए निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी शर्त पूर्व-आवश्यक थी?
o: States with an allotment of 52 seats in the Council of States should agree to join, and their population should be 50% of the total population of Indian states
All princely states were mandated to join without exception
The federal legislature had to be composed entirely of elected members
The British Parliament had to dissolve the viceroy's executive council
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1935 Act proposed a federation comprising provinces and princely states. However, it was conditional: states holding 52 seats in the Council of States had to join, and they had to represent 50% of the total population of all Indian states. These conditions remained unfulfilled, and the federation never materialized.

qe: Under the 1935 Act, subjects at the federal level were divided into 'Reserved' and 'Transferred'. Which of the following was categorized as a 'Reserved' subject?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के तहत, संघीय स्तर पर विषयों को 'आरक्षित' और 'हस्तांतरित' में विभाजित किया गया था। निम्नलिखित में से किसे 'आरक्षित' विषय के रूप में वर्गीकृत किया गया था?
o: Foreign affairs and Defence
Education and Health
Local government and Agriculture
Industry and Excise
e: Detailed Explanation: Under the 1935 Act's federal structure, 'Reserved' subjects—such as defence, foreign affairs, tribal areas, and ecclesiastical affairs—were administered by the Governor-General on the advice of executive councillors who were not responsible to the legislature.

qe: The 1935 Act introduced a bicameral legislature at the center. What was the name of the upper house and the lower house respectively?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम ने केंद्र में द्विसदनीय विधायिका की शुरुआत की। ऊपरी सदन और निचले सदन का नाम क्रमशः क्या था?
o: Council of States and Federal Assembly
Senate and House of Representatives
Legislative Council and Assembly
Upper House and Lower Chamber
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1935 Act provided for a bicameral federal legislature: the upper house was known as the Council of States (260 members) and the lower house was known as the Federal Assembly (375 members).

qe: Which of the following was a major drawback of the Government of India Act, 1935, highlighted by nationalists?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1935 की निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी एक बड़ी कमी थी, जिसे राष्ट्रवादियों ने रेखांकित किया था?
o: It was a rigid constitution with no possibility of internal growth as the amendment power was reserved with the British Parliament
It granted complete independence to India instantly
It abolished the communal electorates system entirely
It gave the legislative assembly absolute control over the entire budget
e: Detailed Explanation: The Act was criticized for being highly rigid, as the power to amend it was reserved for the British Parliament, leaving no scope for Indian leaders to modify it based on evolving national needs.

qe: Who famously described the Government of India Act, 1935, as a 'car, all brakes and no engine'?
qh: किसने 1935 के भारत सरकार अधिनियम को 'एक ऐसी कार, जिसमें ब्रेक तो हैं पर इंजन नहीं' (a car, all brakes and no engine) कहकर वर्णित किया था?
o: Jawaharlal Nehru
Mahatma Gandhi
Subhash Chandra Bose
C.R. Das
e: Detailed Explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru described the 1935 Act as a 'car, all brakes and no engine' to highlight that while the Act provided for extensive administrative machinery, the Governor-General's overriding 'safeguards' and 'special responsibilities' effectively blocked any real power for Indians.

qe: What was the primary aim of the 'Individual Satyagraha' launched by Mahatma Gandhi toward the end of 1940?
qh: 1940 के अंत में महात्मा गांधी द्वारा शुरू किए गए 'व्यक्तिगत सत्याग्रह' का प्राथमिक उद्देश्य क्या था?
o: To show that nationalist patience was not due to weakness and to express people's non-interest in the war
To seize the armouries in various districts
To permanently abolish the land revenue system in Bihar
To form a parallel government in the princely states
e: Detailed Explanation: Individual Satyagraha was launched to demonstrate that the nationalist movement's restraint was not a sign of weakness. It aimed to express that Indians were not interested in the war and made no distinction between Nazism and British autocracy.

qe: Who was the first person to offer individual satyagraha in 1940?
qh: 1940 में व्यक्तिगत सत्याग्रह करने वाले पहले व्यक्ति कौन थे?
o: Vinoba Bhave
Jawaharlal Nehru
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Maulana Azad
e: Detailed Explanation: Acharya Vinoba Bhave was the first person chosen by Mahatma Gandhi to offer individual satyagraha, followed by Jawaharlal Nehru as the second.

qe: The 'Delhi Chalo Movement' was associated with which phase of the nationalist struggle?
qh: 'दिल्ली चलो आंदोलन' (Delhi Chalo Movement) राष्ट्रवादी संघर्ष के किस चरण से संबंधित था?
o: Individual Satyagraha
Civil Disobedience Movement
Non-Cooperation Movement
Quit India Movement
e: Detailed Explanation: The Individual Satyagraha involved selected individuals making anti-war declarations and moving toward Delhi to mobilize villagers, which led to it being popularly known as the 'Delhi Chalo Movement'.

qe: Why did Gandhi designate Jawaharlal Nehru as his successor despite their differing temperaments and views on industrialization and religion?
qh: गांधी ने जवाहरलाल नेहरू को अपना उत्तराधिकारी क्यों नामित किया, जबकि औद्योगीकरण और धर्म पर उनके स्वभाव और विचार भिन्न थे?
o: Because Nehru reliably reflected the pluralist, inclusive idea of India that Gandhi stood for
Because Nehru was a close relative of the Gandhi family
Because Nehru was the only leader who supported the return to the ancient caste system
Because Nehru promised to abolish the Indian National Congress upon taking charge
e: Detailed Explanation: Gandhi believed Nehru was the best person to lead because he was a truly all-India leader, admired by women, trusted by Muslims (as a Hindu), and respected in both North and South India, thus embodying the inclusive vision of the nation.

qe: In March 1942, the British government sent the Cripps Mission to India. Who headed this mission?
qh: मार्च 1942 में, ब्रिटिश सरकार ने क्रिप्स मिशन को भारत भेजा। इस मिशन का नेतृत्व किसने किया था?
o: Stafford Cripps
Lord Wavell
Clement Attlee
Lord Mountbatten
e: Detailed Explanation: Stafford Cripps, a left-wing Labourite and a member of the British War Cabinet, was sent to India in March 1942 to seek Indian support for the war effort in exchange for constitutional proposals.

qe: The Cripps Mission offered India 'Dominion Status' with the right to participate in international bodies. Which condition regarding the 'princely states' made the proposal contentious?
qh: क्रिप्स मिशन ने भारत को अंतर्राष्ट्रीय निकायों में भाग लेने के अधिकार के साथ 'डोमिनियन स्टेटस' की पेशकश की। 'देशी रियासतों' (princely states) के संबंध में किस शर्त ने प्रस्ताव को विवादास्पद बना दिया?
o: Members of the constituent assembly would be partly nominated by the princes
Princes would be forced to abolish their thrones and integrate with democratic provinces
Princes would have to fund the entire British war effort
Princes would be granted an absolute veto over the Viceroy's executive council
e: Detailed Explanation: The Congress objected to the Cripps proposal because it envisioned members of the constituent assembly being partly nominated by the princes, rather than elected by the people of those states.

qe: What controversial provision in the Cripps Mission plan provided a blueprint for the partition of India?
qh: क्रिप्स मिशन योजना में किस विवादास्पद प्रावधान ने भारत के विभाजन का खाका प्रदान किया था?
o: The right of any province not willing to join the Union to have a separate constitution and a separate Union
The mandate that all provinces must immediately adopt a common currency
The power granted to the British government to unilaterally annex any state
The requirement for all provinces to report to a central military authority in London
e: Detailed Explanation: The mission proposed that any province not willing to join the Indian Union could form a separate Union and have a separate constitution. This was viewed by the Congress as a clear blueprint for India's partition.

qe: Why did Mahatma Gandhi describe the Cripps Mission proposals as a 'post-dated cheque'?
qh: महात्मा गांधी ने क्रिप्स मिशन के प्रस्तावों को 'पोस्ट-डेटेड चेक' (post-dated cheque) क्यों कहा?
o: Because the offer for independence was linked to an uncertain future after the war, with no immediate transfer of real power
Because the cheque had no monetary value in the Indian banking system
Because the mission failed to acknowledge the existence of the Congress
Because the date on the documents was already expired
e: Detailed Explanation: Gandhi called it a 'post-dated cheque' because the British promises were for the future, 'after the war'. There was no immediate transfer of power or real share in defence, making the offer hollow given the urgency of the situation.

qe: Which of the following was a reason for the failure of the Cripps Mission according to the Indian National Congress?
qh: भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस के अनुसार, क्रिप्स मिशन की विफलता का एक कारण निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा था?
o: The absence of any plan for an immediate transfer of power and lack of a real share in defence
The mission insisted on the immediate integration of all princely states
The mission demanded the surrender of the Congress Working Committee
The mission's refusal to recognize the dominion status offer
e: Detailed Explanation: The Congress was deeply disappointed because the Cripps proposals offered no immediate transfer of power, and the Governor-General retained supreme control over the defence of India, reducing Indian leaders to 'liveried camp followers'.

qe: Who stated the following: 'I have not become His Majesty’s first Minister to preside over the liquidation of the British Empire'?
qh: यह किसने कहा था: 'मैं महामहिम का पहला मंत्री इसलिए नहीं बना हूँ कि ब्रिटिश साम्राज्य के विघटन की अध्यक्षता करूँ'?
o: Winston Churchill
Stafford Cripps
Ramsay MacDonald
Clement Attlee
e: Detailed Explanation: This statement was made by Winston Churchill, the British Prime Minister during the Second World War. It reflected his firm opposition to any significant transfer of power or autonomy to India during his tenure.

qe: Which section of Indian society was notably excluded from the franchise under the 1919 Act but saw increased importance in later reforms?
qh: भारतीय समाज का कौन सा वर्ग 1919 के अधिनियम के तहत मताधिकार से विशेष रूप से बाहर रखा गया था, लेकिन बाद के सुधारों में उसका महत्व बढ़ गया?
o: Women
Zamindars
Business class
Princes
e: Detailed Explanation: While the 1919 Act was limited, it did provide the right to vote to women for the first time in India, although it remained restricted by property and education qualifications.

qe: The 1935 Act introduced provincial autonomy. What happened to the 'dyarchy' system at the provincial level?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम ने प्रांतीय स्वायत्तता (provincial autonomy) की शुरुआत की। प्रांतीय स्तर पर 'द्वैध शासन' (dyarchy) प्रणाली का क्या हुआ?
o: It was abolished and replaced by provincial autonomy
It was expanded to include even more reserved subjects
It was made mandatory for all princely states to adopt
It was transferred to the central legislative assembly
e: Detailed Explanation: One of the key features of the 1935 Act was that it abolished the 'dyarchy' system at the provincial level and granted provinces autonomy and a separate legal identity, allowing provincial governments to function with more independence.

qe: The central legislature created by the 1935 Act for the proposed All India Federation would have had how many members in the Council of States?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम द्वारा प्रस्तावित अखिल भारतीय महासंघ के लिए बनाई गई केंद्रीय विधायिका में राज्य परिषद (Council of States) के कितने सदस्य होने थे?
e: Detailed Explanation: The Council of States was designed to be a 260-member house, while the Federal Assembly (lower house) was to have 375 members, with representation distributed between British Indian provinces and princely states.

qe: In the context of the 1935 Act, what does 'residuary powers' refer to?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के संदर्भ में, 'अवशिष्ट शक्तियों' (residuary powers) का क्या अर्थ है?
o: Powers not explicitly assigned to either the federal or provincial lists, which were vested with the Governor-General
Powers held exclusively by the district judges
Powers of the local municipal councils to levy taxes
Powers held by the British Crown over the Indian treasury
e: Detailed Explanation: Under the 1935 Act, the Governor-General was given 'residuary powers'. This meant that any legislative subject not clearly categorized under the federal, provincial, or concurrent lists fell under the Governor-General's authority.

qe: How were the provinces freed from the oversight of the secretary of state and governor-general under the 1935 Act?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के तहत प्रांतों को राज्य सचिव और गवर्नर-जनरल की निगरानी से कैसे मुक्त किया गया?
o: They derived legal authority directly from the British Crown
They were given the power to declare independence
They were allowed to maintain their own independent armies
They could veto any ordinance issued by the central Governor-General
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1935 Act granted provinces a separate legal identity. They were no longer under the direct superintendence or direction of the Secretary of State or Governor-General, as their legal authority was henceforth derived directly from the British Crown.

qe: What was the main purpose behind the 'carrot and stick' policy of the British regarding political reforms?
qh: राजनीतिक सुधारों के संबंध में अंग्रेजों की 'गाजर और छड़ी' (carrot and stick) नीति के पीछे मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या था?
o: To isolate the extremists by placating the moderates through concessions, and then suppressing the radicals
To grant immediate and absolute freedom to the Indian population
To build a strong national army managed by the Indian National Congress
To abolish the revenue system and make all lands tax-free for peasants
e: Detailed Explanation: The British 'carrot and stick' approach (repress-placate-suppress) was a strategic effort to divide the nationalist movement. By offering some concessions (carrot) to the Moderates, the British aimed to peel them away from the radical Extremists (stick), making the latter easier to suppress.

qe: During the 1930s, the Congress rule in provinces was a major political development. What was a key limitation for these ministries?
qh: 1930 के दशक के दौरान, प्रांतों में कांग्रेस का शासन एक बड़ा राजनीतिक घटनाक्रम था। इन मंत्रालयों के लिए एक प्रमुख सीमा क्या थी?
o: They had limited control over finances and had to contend with the Governor's special powers
They had absolute power to change the central constitution
They were prohibited from passing any laws related to public education
They were legally forced to implement only the rules prescribed by the Muslim League
e: Detailed Explanation: Although the Congress formed ministries, they operated under the 1935 Act's framework. The Governors retained extensive special powers, and ministers lacked full control over the permanent bureaucracy and finances, often leading to friction.

qe: The 'Lee Commission' (1923) was primarily focused on:
qh: 'ली कमीशन' (1923) का प्राथमिक ध्यान किस पर था?
o: Recruitment and conditions of service for the Superior Civil Services in India
The reform of the agricultural taxation system
The development of a unified national primary education syllabus
The abolition of salt tax in the coastal districts
e: Detailed Explanation: The Lee Commission was appointed to look into the working of the Indian Civil Service and the failure to recruit sufficient British personnel, recommending measures to make service conditions more attractive for Europeans.

qe: Under the 1919 Act, the 'secretary of state for India' was paid out of which treasury for the first time?
qh: 1919 के अधिनियम के तहत, 'भारत के राज्य सचिव' का वेतन पहली बार किस खजाने से दिया गया था?
o: British exchequer
Indian revenue
The Tilak Swaraj Fund
The princely states' royal tribute
e: Detailed Explanation: In an attempt to reduce the 'economic drain', the Government of India Act 1919 mandated that the salary and administrative expenses of the Secretary of State for India should be borne by the British exchequer, not the Indian budget.

qe: Which of the following was a reason for the failure of the 'All India Federation' as proposed by the 1935 Act?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम द्वारा प्रस्तावित 'अखिल भारतीय महासंघ' की विफलता का एक कारण निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा था?
o: The required number of princely states did not agree to join the federation
The Indian National Congress declared a full boycott of the federation
The British Parliament refused to provide any funding
The central legislature could not agree on a common currency
e: Detailed Explanation: The federation required states representing at least 50% of the total population of Indian states to join. Since the conditions for the princes to join were not met, the proposed All India Federation never actually came into existence.

qe: What was the main criticism of the 'Communal Award' (1932) by national leaders?
qh: राष्ट्रीय नेताओं द्वारा 'सांप्रदायिक पंचाट' (Communal Award) (1932) की मुख्य आलोचना क्या थी?
o: It sought to divide the Indian nation by granting separate electorates to the depressed classes
It made the Hindu religion the official state religion
It completely abolished the reservation of seats for Muslims
It mandated the immediate payment of a war tax by all citizens
e: Detailed Explanation: The Communal Award extended the policy of separate electorates to the Depressed Classes, which national leaders felt was a deliberate ploy to weaken the nationalist movement by fracturing the Hindu community.

qe: In the 1935 Act, the three lists for legislative power distribution were:
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम में, विधायी शक्ति वितरण के लिए तीन सूचियाँ कौन सी थीं?
o: Federal, Provincial, and Concurrent
Central, State, and District
Executive, Judicial, and Legislative
Official, Non-official, and Special
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1935 Act introduced a three-fold division of legislative powers between the center and the provinces: the Federal List, the Provincial List, and the Concurrent List.

qe: Why was the 1935 Act considered 'reactionary' by many Indian nationalists?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम को कई भारतीय राष्ट्रवादियों द्वारा 'प्रतिक्रियावादी' (reactionary) क्यों माना गया था?
o: Because it provided a rigid constitution that reinforced British control and fostered separatist tendencies
Because it gave full independence to the Princely States
Because it legalized the complete, unconditional transfer of all military forces to the Congress
Because it abolished all forms of taxation inside the Indian provinces
e: Detailed Explanation: Nationalists condemned the Act for its 'safeguards' which maintained British control, its rigid nature, and its expansion of communal electorates, which they argued would promote separatism and undermine national unity.

qe: What role did 'Harijan' weekly, started by Gandhi in 1933, play in his social reform movement?
qh: 1933 में गांधी द्वारा शुरू की गई 'हरिजन' साप्ताहिक पत्रिका ने उनके सामाजिक सुधार आंदोलन में क्या भूमिका निभाई?
o: It was used to propagate his views on the removal of untouchability
It served as the official journal of the Communist Party of India
It focused exclusively on reporting the financial profit margins of the British managing agencies
It campaigned for the expansion of British military recruitment in Bihar
e: Detailed Explanation: 'Harijan' was a crucial media tool that allowed Gandhi to communicate his philosophical arguments against untouchability, educate the public on social reform, and gather support for the Harijan Sevak Sangh.

qe: The 'Linlithgow Commission' of 1928 was appointed to investigate which sector's crisis?
qh: 1928 का 'लिनलिथगो आयोग' (Linlithgow Commission) किस क्षेत्र के संकट की जांच के लिए नियुक्त किया गया था?
o: Indian agriculture
Textile manufacturing
Jute export trade
Foreign managing agencies
e: Detailed Explanation: The Linlithgow Commission was established to inquire into the systemic crisis and the declining productivity of Indian agriculture during the British era.

qe: What was the significance of the 'Individual Satyagraha' move in the history of the 1940 national upsurge?
qh: 1940 के राष्ट्रीय उभार के इतिहास में 'व्यक्तिगत सत्याग्रह' (Individual Satyagraha) कदम का क्या महत्व था?
o: It allowed the Congress to show the British that the Indian people's patience was not weakness
It mandated the total dissolution of the Congress Working Committee
It legally enabled the Viceroy to appoint a military dictator in every province
It achieved total, absolute independence by the end of 1940
e: Detailed Explanation: By choosing a few selected individuals to protest, Gandhi ensured the nationalist movement remained active without risking mass repression during the war, while simultaneously demonstrating that the nation's patience had limits and that it was fundamentally opposed to the imperialist war.

qe: Who designated Jawaharlal Nehru as his chosen successor despite the preference of many other senior leaders?
qh: अनेक अन्य वरिष्ठ नेताओं की प्राथमिकता के बावजूद किसने जवाहरलाल नेहरू को अपना उत्तराधिकारी नामित किया?
o: Mahatma Gandhi
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
C. Rajagopalachari
Maulana Azad
e: Detailed Explanation: Mahatma Gandhi officially designated Nehru as his successor because, despite their differences, he felt Nehru most reliably represented the pluralist, inclusive, and modern vision of India he envisioned.

qe: The 'Muddiman Commission' was set up in 1924 to look into what specific political issue?
qh: 1924 में 'मडिमन आयोग' (Muddiman Commission) का गठन किस विशिष्ट राजनीतिक मुद्दे की जांच के लिए किया गया था?
o: The deadlock within the diarchic (dyarchy) dispensation
The financial corruption within the salt manufacturing guilds
The territorial mapping of the North-West Frontier Province
The recruitment of native clerks in the Bengal railways
e: Detailed Explanation: The Muddiman Committee was appointed to assess the functioning of the dyarchical system introduced by the 1919 Act and identify why it had led to administrative deadlocks.

qe: What did Gandhi mean when he stated, 'Hinduism dies if untouchability lives'?
qh: गांधी ने जब कहा, 'हिंदू धर्म मर जाता है अगर अस्पृश्यता जीवित रहती है', तो उनका क्या तात्पर्य था?
o: That the practice of untouchability was a moral stain that made the survival of a progressive Hindu religion impossible
That all Hindu temples must be destroyed to save the religion
That the caste system was the only way to promote national unity
That the Vedas had explicitly mandated the practice of untouchability for all believers
e: Detailed Explanation: Gandhi believed that untouchability was a perversion and a moral failure that contradicted the essence of Hindu spirituality. He felt that unless this stigma was purged, the religion could not survive as a respected or ethical moral system.

qe: Which of the following was a structural achievement of the Indian leadership regarding the civil service after the enactment of the 1935 Act?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के अधिनियमन के बाद सिविल सेवा के संबंध में भारतीय नेतृत्व की एक संरचनात्मक उपलब्धि क्या थी?
o: The Act allowed for a large share in the administration in the interim period
It mandated that all British officers must resign their posts immediately
It forced the British treasury to pay all salaries of the civil servants in London
It established an independent civil service recruitment commission in every village
e: Detailed Explanation: While the 1935 Act and subsequent negotiations allowed for a greater Indian share in the provincial administration, it did not grant true sovereignty, as the bureaucracy remained largely beyond the reach of elected ministers.

qe: What was the main purpose of the 'Consultative Council of Greater India' proposed by the Simon Commission?
qh: साइमन कमीशन द्वारा प्रस्तावित 'ग्रेटर इंडिया की सलाहकार परिषद' (Consultative Council of Greater India) का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या था?
o: To provide a platform for representatives of both British provinces and princely states to discuss federal issues
To draft the final legal constitution for the independent state of Burma
To manage the tax revenue collection of the central legislative assembly only
To permanently ban the entry of any native Indian into the executive council rooms
e: Detailed Explanation: The commission recognized that India would eventually become a federation. As an intermediate step, it proposed a Consultative Council to bridge the administrative differences between the British-governed provinces and the princely states.

qe: What were the '1935 safeguards' and why were they criticized by the nationalists?
qh: 1935 के 'सुरक्षा उपाय' (safeguards) क्या थे और राष्ट्रवादियों द्वारा उनकी आलोचना क्यों की गई?
o: They were overarching executive powers given to the Governor to protect British interests, which acted as brakes on the reforms
They were financial protections for the poor subsistence peasantry
They were the names of new welfare schools opened by the Congress ministries
They were judicial decrees that granted absolute independence to all lower courts
e: Detailed Explanation: The 'safeguards' were special executive powers granted to the Governor and Governor-General to interfere in legislation, block bills, or take over administration. Nationalists argued these were not for India's welfare, but to protect British influence and 'brakes' on the limited reforms offered.

qe: What did the inclusion of 'provincial autonomy' signify in the 1935 Act's administrative vision?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के प्रशासनिक दृष्टिकोण में 'प्रांतीय स्वायत्तता' (provincial autonomy) को शामिल करने का क्या अर्थ था?
o: Provinces were given a separate legal identity and freed from the superintendence of the central government
Provinces were given the absolute right to declare war on neighboring countries
Provinces were legally forced to adopt a uniform military code issued by the Governor-General
Provinces were allowed to print their own independent fiat currency notes
e: Detailed Explanation: Provincial autonomy meant that provinces were no longer under the direct administrative 'superintendence and direction' of the central government. They gained a separate legal existence, and their executive and financial authority was derived directly from the British Crown.

qe: Which of the following describes the nature of the electorate system introduced by the 1935 Act for the provincial legislatures?
qh: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा 1935 के अधिनियम द्वारा प्रांतीय विधानसभाओं के लिए शुरू की गई निर्वाचक प्रणाली की प्रकृति का वर्णन करता है?
o: Communal Award based separate electorates were maintained, and the franchise was significantly expanded
The system of separate electorates was entirely replaced by a uniform adult franchise
It allowed only those who owned land worth 50,000 rupees to vote
It mandated that every voter must be a university graduate
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1935 Act maintained and entrenched the divisive communal electorates system. However, it also significantly expanded the franchise, notably granting women the right to vote on the same basis as men, though still within restrictive property/tax criteria.

qe: Why did the British administration eventually fail to establish the 'All India Federation' envisioned by the 1935 Act?
qh: ब्रिटिश प्रशासन अंततः 1935 के अधिनियम द्वारा परिकल्पित 'अखिल भारतीय महासंघ' की स्थापना करने में क्यों विफल रहा?
o: The required participation of the princely states was not achieved due to the strict conditions attached to their entry
The Indian National Congress refused to allow the participation of any state in the federation
The local municipal boards refused to pay the required entry fee
The British Parliament in London voted against the funding of the federal headquarters
e: Detailed Explanation: The federation was a conditional provision. It required princes representing 50% of the total state population to join. The princely rulers remained apprehensive about their sovereignty and largely refused to join on the government's terms, causing the federal provision to remain a dead letter.

qe: The Third Round Table Conference, which directly contributed to the formulation of the Government of India Act 1919 updates, was convened in November 1932. Which significant political entity completely abstained from its proceedings?
qh: नवंबर 1932 में आयोजित तीसरा गोलमेज सम्मेलन, जो भारत सरकार अधिनियम के निर्माण में सहायक बना, में किस महत्वपूर्ण राजनीतिक संस्था ने पूरी तरह से दूरी बनाए रखी थी?
o: The Indian National Congress
The All India Muslim League
The National Liberal Foundation
The Hindu Mahasabha
e: Detailed Explanation: The Third Round Table Conference was held in London in November 1932. Just like the first conference, the Indian National Congress refused to participate, as it was in the midst of the Civil Disobedience civil agitations.

qe: The British Parliament formally enacted the landmark Government of India Act in which month and year?
qh: ब्रिटिश संसद ने किस महीने और वर्ष में ऐतिहासिक भारत सरकार अधिनियम (Government of India Act) को आधिकारिक रूप से पारित किया था?
o: August 1935
November 1932
December 1929
March 1942
e: Detailed Explanation: Following structural discussions across the Round Table Conferences, the British Parliament formally passed the comprehensive Government of India Act in August 1935.

qe: According to the blueprints of the 1935 legislation, the proposed All India Federation was designed to encompass which administrative components?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के खाके के अनुसार, प्रस्तावित अखिल भारतीय महासंघ (All India Federation) में कौन से प्रशासनिक घटक शामिल होने थे?
o: All British Indian provinces, all chief commissioner’s provinces, and the Indian princely states
The three presidency coastal towns of Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras exclusively
The central Imperial Legislative Council zones combined solely with Burma
Only the autonomous states that possessed a separate legal currency registry
e: Detailed Explanation: The Act of 1935 provided for an All India Federation that would dynamically combine all British Indian provinces, all chief commissioner’s provinces, and the sovereign Indian states (princely states) under a single statutory umbrella.

qe: The integration of the Princely States into the proposed 1935 All India Federation was conditional upon them securing what minimum seat threshold within the proposed Council of States?
qh: प्रस्तावित 1935 के अखिल भारतीय महासंघ में रियासतों का शामिल होना उनके द्वारा प्रस्तावित राज्य परिषद (Council of States) में न्यूनतम कितनी सीटों के आवंटन को स्वीकार करने पर निर्भर था?
o: 52 seats
260 seats
141 seats
30 seats
e: Detailed Explanation: The formation of the federation was strictly conditional on princely states being allotted a total minimum of 52 seats inside the upper house (Council of States) agreeing to join the framework.

qe: Apart from legislative seat counts, what demographic condition was mandatory for the princely states to fulfill before the All India Federation of 1935 could be operationalized?
qh: विधायी सीटों के अलावा, 1935 के अखिल भारतीय महासंघ के चालू होने से पहले रियासतों के लिए किस जनसांख्यिकीय शर्त (demographic condition) को पूरा करना अनिवार्य था?
o: The aggregate population of the joining states had to be 50 per cent of the total population of all Indian states
They had to represent exactly 78 million Bengali-speaking residents across territories
The landless agricultural laborers within those states had to possess universal voting rights
Their combined population tracking metric had to match the urban middle classes of Bombay Presidency
e: Detailed Explanation: A key hurdle for the federation was that the aggregate population of the princely states opting to join had to constitute at least 50 per cent of the total collective population of all native Indian states.

qe: Because the princely states refused to fulfill the strict population and seat conditions, the All India Federation never materialized. How did the central government of India continue to operate up to 1946?
qh: चूंकि रियासतों ने जनसंख्या और सीट की शर्तों को पूरा करने से इनकार कर दिया, इसलिए अखिल भारतीय महासंघ कभी अस्तित्व में नहीं आया। इसके कारण भारत की केंद्र सरकार 1946 तक किस अधिनियम के तहत काम करती रही?
o: As per the administrative and executive provisions of the Government of India Act, 1919
Under the unilateral emergency ordinances issued by the Secretary of State based in London
According to the temporary regulatory guidelines introduced by the Metcalfe Act of 1835
As a complete military protectorate directed by the British War Cabinet exclusively
e: Detailed Explanation: Since the required number of princely states defaulted on joining, the federal part of the 1935 Act remained a dead letter. Consequently, the central executive architecture of India continued to function all the way up to 1946 under the older provisions of the Government of India Act 1919.

qe: Which centralized administrative authority was explicitly designated as the absolute 'pivot' of the entire constitutional machinery under the Government of India Act, 1935?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1935 के तहत किस केंद्रीकृत प्रशासनिक प्राधिकारी को पूरे संवैधानिक तंत्र का पूर्ण 'धुरी' (pivot) नामित किया गया था?
o: The Governor-General
The Speaker of the Federal Assembly
The Secretary of State for India
The Chief Justice of the Federal Court
e: Detailed Explanation: The statutory structure of the 1935 Act concentrated ultimate executive authority in one position, making the Governor-General the undisputed pivot of the entire Constitution.

qe: Under the federal executive division of the 1935 Act, which specific portfolio heads were categorized as 'Reserved Subjects' to be managed exclusively by the Governor-General?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के संघीय कार्यकारी विभाजन के तहत, किन विशिष्ट विभागों को 'आरक्षित विषयों' (Reserved Subjects) के रूप में वर्गीकृत किया गया था, जिनका प्रबंधन विशेष रूप से गवर्नर-जनरल द्वारा किया जाना था?
o: Foreign affairs, defence, tribal areas, and ecclesiastical affairs
Education, health, local self-government, and land revenue tracking
Customs tariffs, currency valuation, and corporate textile protection metrics
Law and order, public finance, and mass technical industrial education
e: Detailed Explanation: The Act divided administrative portfolios into two bands. The critical 'Reserved Subjects' comprised foreign affairs, defence, tribal areas, and ecclesiastical affairs, keeping them under the exclusive control of the Governor-General.

qe: How did the constitutional position of the Executive Councillors who advised the Governor-General on 'Reserved Subjects' differ from that of popular ministers?
qh: आरक्षित विषयों पर गवर्नर-जनरल को सलाह देने वाले 'कार्यकारी पार्षदों' (Executive Councillors) की संवैधानिक स्थिति लोकप्रिय मंत्रियों से किस प्रकार भिन्न थी?
o: They were completely insulated from legislative oversight and were not responsible to the central legislature
They were elected directly via universal adult franchise across all British provinces
They were legally forced to resign if the lower house passed a vote of no-confidence
They were subordinated to the popular ministers headed by a provincial premier
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1935 Act maintained a non-democratic core at the center. The executive councillors who managed the reserved portfolios were bureaucratic nominees who were explicitly not responsible or answerable to the central legislature.

qe: Under the 1935 Act, the 'Transferred Subjects' at the federal level were to be administered by the Governor-General on the advice of ministers who faced which constitutional condition?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के तहत, संघीय स्तर पर 'हस्तांतरित विषयों' (Transferred Subjects) का प्रशासन गवर्नर-जनरल द्वारा उन मंत्रियों की सलाह पर किया जाना था, जिन्हें किस संवैधानिक शर्त का सामना करना पड़ता था?
o: They were responsible to the federal legislature and were legally forced to resign on losing its confidence
They were nominated directly by the Chamber of Princes based on population strength
They held permanent, lifetime tenures that were completely insulated from any legislative vote
They were paid entirely out of the British exchequer in London to prevent economic drain
e: Detailed Explanation: Ministers who managed the Transferred subjects were elected members chosen from the legislature. They were constitutionally responsible to the federal legislature and had to resign if they lost the confidence of that legislative body.

qe: What executive parameter allowed the Governor-General to completely bypass ministerial advice and act independently under his own authority under the 1935 Act framework?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के तहत किस कार्यकारी नियम ने गवर्नर-जनरल को मंत्रिस्तरीय सलाह को पूरी तरह से दरकिनार करने और स्वतंत्र रूप से काम करने की अनुमति दी थी?
o: Acting in his individual judgement for the discharge of his special responsibilities regarding security and tranquillity
Securing a direct judicial warrant signed by three judges panel of the High Court
Filing a written petition cleared by a majority of the provincial elected premiums
Invoking the historical maritime navigation rules passed during Wellesley's administration
e: Detailed Explanation: The Act armed the Governor-General with wide discretionary limits. He was statutorily authorized to act under his own 'individual judgement' to fulfill his special responsibilities for safeguarding the security and tranquillity of India.

qe: The central bicameral legislature designed by the Government of India Act, 1935, was composed of which two houses?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1935 द्वारा तैयार की गई केंद्रीय द्विसदनीय विधायिका किन दो सदनों से मिलकर बनी थी?
o: The Council of States (upper house) and the Federal Assembly (lower house)
The House of Representatives (lower house) and the Senate (upper house)
The Central Legislative Assembly and the Imperial Advisory Board
The Chamber of Princes and the Provincial Councils division
e: Detailed Explanation: The legislative architecture at the federal level was designed to be bicameral, containing an upper chamber named the Council of States and a lower chamber named the Federal Assembly.

qe: Under the structural layout of the 260-member Council of States, what percentage of seats was reserved to be nominated directly by the princely rulers?
qh: 260 सदस्यीय काउंसिल ऑफ स्टेट्स (Council of States) के संरचनात्मक ढांचे के तहत, कितने प्रतिशत सीटें सीधे रियासतों के शासकों द्वारा मनोनीत की जानी थीं?
o: 40 per cent
One-third (33 per cent)
50 per cent
14 per cent
e: Detailed Explanation: The 260 seats of the upper house were split to integrate conservative elements. While a portion was elected from British provinces, exactly 40 per cent of the total members were to be nominated directly by the princes.

qe: The lower house, or the Federal Assembly, was structured to feature 375 members. What specific fraction of this house was designated to be nominated by the native princes?
qh: निचले सदन, या फेडरल असेंबली (Federal Assembly) में 375 सदस्य होने थे। इस सदन का कितना विशिष्ट हिस्सा देशी राजकुमारों द्वारा मनोनीत किया जाना तय किया गया था?
o: One-third
Forty per cent
Half
Ten per cent
e: Detailed Explanation: To check progressive nationalist forces in the lower house, the 375-member Federal Assembly had a substantial non-elected block: exactly one-third of its total membership was to be nominated by the autocratic princes.

qe: What paradoxical structural feature characterized the election methodology fixed for the two central houses under the 1935 Act framework?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के तहत दोनों केंद्रीय सदनों के लिए तय की गई चुनाव पद्धति की कौन सी विरोधाभासी संरचनात्मक विशेषता थी?
o: Election to the Council of States was direct, while election to the Federal Assembly was indirect
Election to both houses was based entirely on universal adult franchise tracking
The Federal Assembly members were elected directly, while the upper house was entirely nominated
Both houses relied strictly on indirect selection via local village panchayats exclusively
e: Detailed Explanation: Paradoxically, the 1935 Act flipped standard parliamentary norms. It introduced a direct election methodology for the upper chamber (Council of States) and an indirect election process for the lower house (Federal Assembly).

qe: What operational tenure and retirement parameters were fixed for the upper chamber (Council of States) under the 1935 Act directives?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के तहत उच्च सदन (Council of States) के लिए कौन से परिचालन कार्यकाल और सेवानिवृत्ति के मानदंड तय किए गए थे?
o: It was a permanent body with one-third of its members retiring every third year
It held a fixed non-renewable tenure of 5 years for all members simultaneously
It was subject to arbitrary dissolution by the Premier every single year
It had a continuous 7-year cycle with half of its members retiring every second year
e: Detailed Explanation: The Council of States was structured as a permanent legislative body. It was not subject to dissolution, and its stability was maintained by having one-third of its total members retire every third year.

qe: Under the legislative power schedules of the 1935 Act, which specific branch of the central legislature held the exclusive authority to move a vote of no-confidence against ministers?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के विधायी शक्ति नियमों के तहत, केंद्रीय विधायिका की किस विशिष्ट शाखा के पास मंत्रियों के खिलाफ अविश्वास प्रस्ताव लाने का विशेष अधिकार था?
o: The Federal Assembly
The Council of States
The Governor's Executive Board
The Chamber of Princes
e: Detailed Explanation: The Act distributed powers unequally between the chambers. Only the members of the lower house (Federal Assembly) were armed with the power to move a vote of no-confidence against ministers, while the Council of States held no such power.

qe: What extraordinary financial parameter illustrates the complete lack of legislative sovereignty over public finance under the 1935 central legislative framework?
qh: कौन सा असाधारण वित्तीय पैमाना 1935 के केंद्रीय विधायी ढांचे के तहत सार्वजनिक वित्त पर विधायी संप्रभुता की पूर्ण कमी को दर्शाता है?
o: Exactly 80 per cent of the total central budget remained completely non-votable
The legislators were entirely barred from discussing any land revenue items
The entire public finance framework had to be cleared by the London exchequer manually
Indian ministers held zero authority to ask any supplementary financial questions
e: Detailed Explanation: Although parliamentary forms were displayed, the central legislature's control over expenditure was blocked: exactly 80 per cent of the total federal budget remained entirely non-votable by the members.

qe: The 1935 legislative framework split powers into three lists: federal, provincial, and concurrent. Who was legally endowed with the ultimate 'residuary powers' of legislation?
qh: 1935 के विधायी ढांचे ने शक्तियों को तीन सूचियों (संघीय, प्रांतीय और समवर्ती) में विभाजित किया। कानून बनाने की अंतिम 'अवशिष्ट शक्तियाँ' (residuary powers) कानूनी रूप से किसे प्रदान की गई थीं?
o: The Governor-General
The Speaker of the Federal Assembly
The British Parliament in London directly
The Premier heading the Council of Ministers
e: Detailed Explanation: In the federal legislative mapping of lists, any residual subject that was not explicitly noted inside the three charts was placed under the authority of the Governor-General.

qe: Apart from residuary powers, what overriding financial authority did the Governor-General hold regarding budget allocations inside the central legislature?
qh: अवशिष्ट शक्तियों के अलावा, केंद्रीय विधायिका के भीतर बजट आवंटन के संबंध में गवर्नर-जनरल के पास कौन सा सर्वोपरि वित्तीय अधिकार सुरक्षित था?
o: He held the sovereign power to restore cuts in grants executed by the legislature
He could completely liquidate all corporate tax deposits to clear the public debt
He held the right to levy an automatic 50% tariff surcharge on native khadi workshops
He was legally forced to route 100% of his financial decisions to the Constituent Assembly
e: Detailed Explanation: The Governor-General retained a strong grip over public finance. Even if the legislature voted to cut or reduce specific financial grants, he held the overriding power to restore those cuts to protect colonial interests.

qe: Under the structural shifts introduced in the third section of the 1935 Act, what system formally replaced the unworkable framework of 'Dyarchy' at the provincial level?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के तीसरे खंड में शुरू किए गए संरचनात्मक बदलावों के तहत, प्रांतीय स्तर पर 'द्वैध शासन' (Dyarchy) के अव्यवहारिक ढांचे के स्थान पर कौन सी प्रणाली औपचारिक रूप से लागू की गई थी?
o: Provincial Autonomy
Bicameral Federalism
Centralized Direct Rule
Saptanga Decentralization Mappings
e: Detailed Explanation: At the provincial level, the 1935 Act introduced a significant structural change: it completely abolished the dual-rule system of Dyarchy and replaced it with 'Provincial Autonomy'.

qe: Following the introduction of Provincial Autonomy, how was the statutory legal relationship between the provinces and the central authorities modified?
qh: प्रांतीय स्वायत्तता की शुरुआत के बाद, प्रांतों और केंद्रीय अधिकारियों के बीच वैधानिक कानूनी संबंध को कैसे संशोधित किया गया था?
o: Provinces were freed from the superintendence of the Governor-General and derived legal authority directly from the British Crown
Provinces were completely subordinated to a specialized three-judge panel of the central assembly
The provincial administrations lost their separate legal identities and financial powers completely
Provinces were legally forced to route all their legislative codes to the Federal Assembly Speaker
e: Detailed Explanation: Under the autonomy model, provinces were granted a separate legal identity. They were formally freed from the administrative 'superintendence and direction' of both the Secretary of State and the Governor-General, deriving their legal authority directly from the British Crown.

qe: What independent financial power was granted to the provincial governments to sustain their autonomous administrative structure under the 1935 framework?
qh: 1935 के ढांचे के तहत प्रांतीय सरकारों को अपने स्वायत्त प्रशासनिक ढांचे को बनाए रखने के लिए कौन सी स्वतंत्र वित्तीय शक्ति प्रदान की गई थी?
o: The independent power to borrow money on their own security
The absolute right to print independent regional paper currencies without central guidelines
The power to levy a flat 100% transit custom tariff on all incoming British textile shipments
Complete control to reallocate 80% of the central budget grants to local village boards
e: Detailed Explanation: To provide financial backing to autonomy, provinces were given independent financial powers and resources, which explicitly included the right to borrow money directly on their own security.

qe: Under the provincial executive guidelines of the 1935 Act, the Governor was designated as the nominee and representative of which authority?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के प्रांतीय कार्यकारी दिशानिर्देशों के तहत, राज्यपाल को किस प्राधिकारी का नामांकित व्यक्ति और प्रतिनिधि नामित किया गया था?
o: The British Crown
The Central Legislative Assembly majority
The Congress Working Committee executive panel
The Chief Justice of the newly consolidated Federal Court
e: Detailed Explanation: The provincial executive was headed by the Governor, who was explicitly designated as the Crown's direct nominee and representative, exercising executive authority on the King's behalf within that province.

qe: What extraordinary administrative power did the provincial Governor retain under the 1935 Act if he deemed that local governance had broken down?
qh: यदि प्रांतीय राज्यपाल को लगता था कि स्थानीय शासन विफल हो गया है, तो 1935 के अधिनियम के तहत उसके पास कौन सा असाधारण प्रशासनिक अधिकार था?
o: He could completely take over and indefinitely run the provincial administration under his own authority
He had the right to petition the Federal Assembly to dissolve the British Cabinet in London
He could automatically liquidate all corporate land assets held by the local zamindars
He was legally forced to surrender his entire council to the popular ministerial premiers
e: Detailed Explanation: The Governor held wide emergency powers. If local governance broken down, he could use his special powers to completely take over and indefinitely run the entire provincial administration under his own authority.

qe: Under the provincial legislative updates of the 1935 Act, how were the members of the local provincial legislatures to be chosen?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के प्रांतीय विधायी सुधारों के तहत, स्थानीय प्रांतीय विधानसभाओं के सदस्यों का चयन कैसे किया जाना था?
o: All members were to be directly elected via an expanded franchise framework
They were to be indirectly filtered through a multi-layered tier of local body sieves
One-third were elected, while the remaining majority was nominated by the Chamber of Princes
They were handpicked by the executive councillors of the central Governor-General directly
e: Detailed Explanation: Reversing the indirect system attached to the center, the provincial legislatures were structured on democratic lines where all members were to be directly elected by the population under an expanded franchise.

qe: Regarding the administration of local affairs, the provincial subjects were to be managed by ministers in a Council of Ministers headed by which official?
qh: स्थानीय मामलों के प्रशासन के संबंध में, प्रांतीय विषयों का प्रबंधन मंत्रियों द्वारा एक मंत्रिपरिषद में किया जाना था, जिसका प्रमुख कौन सा अधिकारी होता था?
o: A Premier
The Governor-General
The Speaker of the Assembly
The Chief Commissioner
e: Detailed Explanation: Under provincial autonomy, elected ministers were responsible for administering all provincial subjects within a coordinated council of ministers, which was headed by a popular leader designated as the Premier.

qe: What financial parameter illustrates that provincial autonomy remained restricted under the 1935 Act public finance framework?
qh: कौन सा वित्तीय पैमाना यह दर्शाता है कि 1935 के अधिनियम के सार्वजनिक वित्त ढांचे के तहत प्रांतीय स्वायत्तता सीमित बनी रही?
o: Exactly 40 per cent of the provincial budget was still kept non-votable
The provincial legislatures were completely barred from passing any tax laws
The entire provincial revenue collection had to be sent to the center within a week
Indian ministers held zero authority to allocate funds for health and education
